At Husky TechnologiesTM, our success is based on your success. Our ability to keep our customers in the lead is based on building the strongest team possible.

Husky TechnologiesTM has a strong foundation built on innovation, close customer relationships and a unique culture and values. We are dedicated to offering our customers the highest quality products and services and are looking for people with the inspiration and talent to develop with us as we pursue our ambitious growth strategy. We are a leader in developing state-of-the-art technology and it is this technology base that uniquely positions us to serve customers who seek differentiation through solutions that provide speed, flexibility and maximum productivity. This capability is at the core of our mission and competitive strategy.

Husky TechnologiesTM offers a wealth of opportunity for personal growth and development. Most importantly, Husky Technologies TM offers an opportunity to work with – and be challenged by – a team of great people. Our success is possible because of the creativity, intelligence and passion of our people around the world and their desire to lead change. At the same time, we are not afraid to expect a lot and strive for leadership in all of our key markets. We are a company taking on new challenges and for the right people this means exceptional career development opportunities, the chance to be part of a team that is the best in the world at what we do and the experience that comes from working in an environment that demands constant transformation and innovation.

Husky TechnologiesTM is an exciting company with tremendous potential. We have a great team and great expectations. If you are attracted to bold goals, believe in uncompromising honesty, support mutual respect, care about environmental responsibility, have a passion for excellence and a desire to make a positive contribution – then we want you to join the Husky TechnologiesTM team!

The Finance Director serves as a strategic business partner to the Leadership Team in support of Husky’s Global Service Business and Customer Success Management strategy. This role provides leadership for financial planning, forecasting, performance analysis, governance, and decision support to drive profitable growth, improve operational performance, and strengthen financial visibility across service revenue streams, including field service, contracts, parts, and other aftermarket offerings. The Finance Director is expected to influence strategic decisions, lead transformation initiatives, and build a high-performing finance capability that enables the business to scale effectively.

Key Responsibilities

Financial Planning & Forecasting

Lead the annual budget, quarterly forecast, and long-range planning processes for the service business.
Develop robust revenue, margin, cost, and headcount forecasts based on operational and commercial drivers.
Translate business strategies into financial plans with clear assumptions, risks, and opportunities.
Support scenario planning and sensitivity analysis for service growth, pricing, labor utilization, and investment decisions.

Performance Management & Analysis

Deliver timely and accurate monthly financial reporting and variance analysis for service revenue, gross margin, SG&A, and operating income.
Analyze business performance by region, product line, customer segment, channel, and service offering.
Monitor and explain key drivers of performance, including labor utilization, absorption, contract profitability, attach rates, response times, and service productivity.
Provide actionable insights and recommendations to improve growth, profitability, and working capital performance.

Business Partnering

Serve as the senior finance partner to service leadership, operations, commercial teams, and Customer Success leaders, providing insight and challenge on strategic priorities, business performance, and investment decisions.
Lead financial evaluation of pricing strategies, contract renewals, service program design, and capital or operating investments to support sustainable growth and margin expansion.
Provide proactive challenge and decision support to business leaders by identifying risks, opportunities, and trade-offs across growth, productivity, service delivery, and resource allocation.
Lead cross-functional evaluation of new service offerings, business models, and transformation initiatives that improve service coverage, utilization, fulfillment, cost efficiency, and customer value.
Sponsor finance and business transformation initiatives across Finance and Customer Success Management, including enhancements to processes, reporting, operating metrics, and decision frameworks that support growth, profitability, and scalability.

Management Reporting & KPI Development

Develop and enhance dashboards, reporting tools, and KPIs that improve transparency and decision-making.
Standardize definitions and reporting for critical service metrics across the organization.
Improve reporting automation and self-service analytics capabilities where possible.
Present clear financial results and business insights to senior leadership

Process Improvement & Governance

Strengthen forecasting accuracy, reporting discipline, and financial controls within the service business.
Drive continuous improvement in FP&A processes, planning models, and reporting frameworks.
Ensure alignment with corporate finance requirements, accounting policies, and internal controls
Support month-end close and planning processes in partnership with accounting and finance teams.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or a related field required.
CPA, CMA, CFA, or MBA preferred.
10+ years of progressive experience in FP&A, finance business partnering, commercial finance, or operational finance, including leadership responsibility.
Experience in a service, aftermarket, field service, maintenance, or contract-based business strongly preferred.
Strong financial modeling, forecasting, and business analysis skills.
Advanced proficiency in Excel and experience with ERP and planning/reporting systems.
Executive presence with strong communication, presentation, and stakeholder management skills, and the ability to influence senior leaders across functions and regions.
Proven ability to work cross-functionally in a fast-paced, performance-driven environment

Preferred Experience In a Service Business

Understanding of service revenue models such as time and materials, service contracts, preventive maintenance, subscriptions, and parts/service bundles.
Experience analyzing operational KPIs such as technician utilization, service efficiency, contract margins, backlog, renewal rates, and service attach rates.
Familiarity with pricing strategy, labor productivity, installed base analytics, and customer lifecycle economics

Core Competencies

Strategic leadership
Financial and commercial acumen
Analytical rigor
Executive business partnership
Influence and executive communication
Problem solving
Process improvement
Results orientation and a bias for action

Team Development

Build and lead a high-performing finance team with strong capability in financial analysis, strategic thinking, business partnership, and change leadership.
Lead, coach, and develop team members, including succession planning, capability building, and development of future finance leaders.

Financial Leadership

Provide consistent, timely, accurate, and decision-oriented financial reporting for the service business, with greater automation and self-service access to insights where possible

Summary

Are you a high-energy finance leader with a talent for navigating complex commercial landscapes and driving strategic growth?

We are seeking a Commercial Finance Director to provide pivotal commercial support for a high-growth portfolio within our Connectivity & Cloud Solutions (CCS) segment. This portfolio of accounts is projected to increase significantly in 2027 and beyond, and this role is critical to managing the financial and operational success of new and existing large customers. In this hyper-growth environment, you will have the unique opportunity to shape the financial trajectory of our fastest-scaling accounts.

You will act as a key business partner, managing the commercial aspects as well as the full P&L for some of the largest accounts in Celestica. You will bridge the gap between finance, supply chain, engineering, and executive leadership to ensure profitable execution and strategic alignment.

Detailed Description

Performs tasks such as, but not limited to, the following:

Commercial Leadership: Lead all commercial aspects for assigned high-growth customers, including contract management, pricing discussions, and the implementation of service elements.
Strategic Planning & Forecasting: Drive the finalization of the Annual Operating Plan (AOP), 3-year Strategic Plan (SP), and monthly financial forecasts for the Global Customer Business Unit (GCBU).
Executive Reporting: Prepare and present frequent updates to the Executive Leadership Team (ELT) (monthly or bi-weekly) regarding portfolio performance, risks, and opportunities.
Cross-Functional Collaboration: Partner with customer, sales and production teams to ensure financial readiness for new product introductions and large-scale bookings.
Financial Analysis: Perform quantitative and qualitative analysis to support key customer negotiations and drive cash or profit improvements.
Global Coordination: Manage financial expectations and solutions across multiple international manufacturing sites to ensure alignment on forecasts and outlooks.

Knowledge/Skills/Competencies

Strategic Business Partnering: Proven ability to influence and negotiate effectively across cross-functional teams, including Supply Chain, Engineering, and GCBU leaders.
Commercial Acumen: Expertise in managing complex commercial elements such as contracts, pricing strategies, and unique deal constructs.
Analytical Excellence: Exceptional attention to detail with the ability to decipher key dynamics influencing financial results and pinpointing areas for margin enhancement.
Communication: Skilled at communicating complex financial data and strategic outlooks to the ELT, the customer and other external stakeholders.
Adaptability: Adept at managing multiple complex initiatives under tight deadlines within a dynamic, global environment spanning multiple international sites.

Physical Demands

Duties of this position are performed in a normal office environment
Duties may require extended periods of sitting and sustained visual concentration on a computer monitor or on numbers and other detailed data
Repetitive manual movements are frequently required (e.g. data entry, using a computer mouse, using a calculator, etc)
Occasional overnight travel is required

Typical Experience

10+ years of progressive, relevant finance experience.
Commercial finance experience is strongly preferred.

Typical Education

Bachelor’s degree in Finance or Accounting.
CPA or equivalent accounting designation is preferred.

This job description is not intended to be an exhaustive list of all duties and responsibilities of the position. Employees are held accountable for all duties of the job. Job duties and the % of time identified for any function are subject to change at any time.

Celestica, Inc. (NYSE: CLS; TSX: CLS) is a technology leader dedicated to driving customer success and market advancements. With deep expertise in design, engineering, manufacturing, supply chain, and platform solutions, Celestica enables critical data center infrastructure for AI, cloud, and hybrid cloud and advances technologies in high-growth markets. Advanced Excel skills and experience working with ERP systems and financial reporting applications.

jobs.title: Interim Director, Procurement
jobs.description:
IMMEDIATE INTERIM OPPORTUNITY

Interim Director, Procurement

Reports to: Associate Vice-President, Finance

Location: Virtual

Duration: 6 Months

Our client, a large and complex Canadian academic institution, is seeking an experienced Interim Director, Procurement for an initial six-month mandate.

The organization is looking for a seasoned procurement leader who can provide strong operational leadership while bringing the experience, perspective and confidence to challenge existing thinking, act as a positive disruptor and elevate the overall value, impact and reputation of Procurement across the institution.

Reporting to the Associate Vice-President, Finance and leading a team of five, the Interim Director will ensure the continued effective operation of the procurement function while helping the organization consider how Procurement can become a more strategic, progressive and value-adding partner to the broader institution.

The successful interim will bring credibility as both an experienced procurement operator and strategic advisor. They will engage and develop the existing team, build stronger relationships with internal stakeholders, challenge established practices where appropriate, and identify opportunities to improve processes, technology, supplier management, organizational risk and financial value.

THE MANDATE

The Interim Director will assume leadership of the procurement function and provide stability, direction and mentorship to the team through a period of transition.

A significant component of the mandate will be to examine how Procurement is positioned and experienced across the organization. The Interim Director will work closely with stakeholders to demystify procurement, simplify how internal clients navigate centralized procurement and build greater understanding of the value that an effective procurement function can bring to the institution.

This is not simply about maintaining the existing procurement operation. The Interim Director will be expected to challenge current approaches, identify opportunities for improvement and leave the function stronger, more professional and better positioned for the future.

KEY PRIORITIES

Operational Leadership and Team Development

Provide hands-on leadership and oversight of the procurement function and its team of five.
Ensure continuity and effective delivery of procurement activities throughout the six-month transition.
Engage, coach and support team members, bringing additional procurement expertise, knowledge and external perspective into the function.
Assess current capabilities, ways of working and opportunities to strengthen the effectiveness and professionalism of the team.
Create clarity around priorities, accountability and service expectations.

Strategic Procurement Leadership

Assess the current procurement operating model and identify opportunities to elevate Procurement from primarily a transactional function to a more strategic enterprise partner.
Develop or refine the procurement strategy and establish clear priorities for improving value, service, governance and organizational impact.
Challenge existing practices and conventional thinking, bringing external best practices and practical ideas from other large, complex organizations.
Identify opportunities to generate measurable financial and non-financial value through improved sourcing, vendor management, demand management and procurement practices.

Stakeholder Engagement and Procurement Brand

Build strong relationships across a complex academic and administrative stakeholder environment.
Improve stakeholders’ understanding of when, why and how Procurement should be engaged.
Demystify procurement policies and processes and make the function easier to navigate for internal clients.
Strengthen the internal brand and credibility of Procurement by positioning the team as pragmatic business partners rather than simply a control or compliance function.
Educate stakeholders on procurement responsibilities, processes, policies and the value of early Procurement involvement.

Policy, Process and Governance

Review existing procurement policies, procedures and governance structures and identify opportunities for modernization and simplification.
Establish clearer, more user-friendly processes that balance strong governance and risk management with an effective stakeholder experience.
Identify unnecessary complexity, duplication or friction within existing procurement processes.
Strengthen transparency, consistency and accountability across procurement decision-making.

Technology and Procurement Enablement

Review how technology is currently being leveraged across the procurement function and identify opportunities to improve efficiency, visibility and user experience.
Review the institution’s current purchase card program, associated technology and vendor arrangements and identify opportunities to improve functionality, controls, adoption and organizational value.
Assess whether existing procurement technology and processes are delivering sufficient value and identify opportunities for improvement or modernization.
Consider how automation, analytics and emerging technologies could enable a more efficient and insight-driven procurement function.

Strategic Sourcing and Collaboration

Review key supplier relationships and sourcing strategies to identify opportunities to generate additional savings and organizational value.
Explore collaborative procurement and group-buying opportunities with universities and other broader public sector organizations across Canada.
Identify areas where increased purchasing leverage, category management or consolidated sourcing could deliver improved commercial outcomes.
Bring an external market perspective on procurement models, technologies, supplier strategies and emerging practices.

Risk and Supply Chain Transparency

Assess procurement and supply-chain risks across the institution and identify areas where governance, visibility or controls could be strengthened.
Improve transparency across key supplier relationships, contractual commitments and supply-chain dependencies.
Consider emerging risks related to supplier concentration, continuity of supply, compliance, cybersecurity, sustainability and broader geopolitical or economic disruption.
Ensure procurement decisions appropriately balance financial value, service, risk and institutional requirements.

IDEAL EXPERIENCE

The successful interim will be a seasoned procurement executive who has previously led procurement within a large, complex and highly stakeholder-driven organization.

Significant senior procurement leadership experience, ideally 15+ years across progressively responsible procurement, strategic sourcing and supply-chain roles.
Previous experience leading a procurement function within a university, college, healthcare organization, government entity, Crown corporation or another broader public sector organization.
A strong understanding of public-sector procurement principles, governance, competitive procurement, accountability and transparency.
Demonstrated success developing and implementing procurement strategies that have delivered measurable savings, value creation and service improvement.
Experience transforming or elevating a procurement function beyond transactional execution toward a more strategic business-partner model.
Strong experience with procurement technology, e-procurement, purchase cards, spend analytics and technology-enabled process improvement.
Experience evaluating vendors, commercial arrangements and procurement platforms and challenging whether existing solutions continue to provide appropriate value.
Demonstrated ability to review and improve procurement policies, processes and governance without creating unnecessary bureaucracy.
Strong strategic sourcing, contract negotiation and supplier management experience.
Experience exploring collaborative procurement, consortium purchasing or group-buying arrangements would be highly valuable.
A track record of strengthening procurement teams through coaching, knowledge transfer, capability development and improved ways of working.
Exceptional stakeholder engagement skills with an ability to influence senior leaders and build credibility across decentralized and complex environments.
Experience working effectively in environments where stakeholder education, relationship building and change management are critical to improving the adoption of centralized procurement.

LEADERSHIP PROFILE

This mandate will suit a senior procurement leader who combines practical operational capability with strategic perspective.

They will be comfortable getting close enough to the work to understand what is happening while resisting the temptation to simply operate the existing model. They will ask difficult questions, constructively challenge established practices and bring solutions grounded in experience from other complex organizations.

The successful interim will be:
A positive disruptor who is comfortable challenging the status quo while bringing stakeholders with them.
Pragmatic and commercially minded, with a strong orientation toward measurable value.
Comfortable operating within the governance and accountability requirements of a broader public sector environment.
Collaborative and highly credible with senior stakeholders.
An effective coach who enjoys developing people and transferring knowledge.
Curious and externally focused, bringing ideas, benchmarks and best practices into the organization.
Able to balance strategy with execution and quickly identify where the greatest opportunities for improvement exist.
Skilled at simplifying complexity and making procurement easier for stakeholders to understand and navigate.

OUTCOMES

At the conclusion of the six-month mandate, the organization should have:

A stable, engaged and effectively led procurement team.
A clearer strategic direction and priorities for the procurement function.
Improved stakeholder understanding of Procurement and a stronger internal reputation for the function.
More effective and user-friendly procurement policies and processes.
Identified opportunities for measurable savings and increased organizational value.
A clearer roadmap for procurement technology and improved utilization of current systems.
Recommendations regarding the purchase card program, technology and vendor arrangements.
Greater visibility into supplier and supply-chain risk.
Identified opportunities for collaborative procurement and group purchasing with peer institutions.
Increased procurement capability through coaching and knowledge transfer to the existing team.
Practical recommendations for the future operating model, capabilities and leadership requirements of the procurement function.

This is an opportunity for an experienced procurement executive to make a meaningful impact over a relatively short period: stabilizing the function today while helping define what a more strategic, progressive and value-adding procurement function should look like for the future.

Au moins 10 ans d’expérience avec des responsabilités croissantes en transformation des activités, en exécution de la stratégie, en conception de modèles opérationnels, en excellence commerciale, en direction de programmes d’entreprise ou en conseil en gestion.
Baccalauréat ou maîtrise en administration des affaires, en génie, en stratégie, en gestion des opérations, en systèmes d’information ou dans une discipline connexe.
Expérience dans un rôle interne en stratégie, en transformation, en excellence opérationnelle ou en consultation.
Expérience démontrée dans la direction de transformations complexes et interfonctionnelles touchant plusieurs régions géographiques ou unités d’affaires.
Capacité éprouvée à rallier les parties prenantes de la haute direction et les fonctions autour de priorités communes, sans s’appuyer sur une autorité hiérarchique directe.
Expérience dans la traduction de la stratégie en feuilles de route réalisables, en structures de gouvernance, en mécanismes opérationnels et en résultats mesurables.
Solide sens des affaires et capacité à relier la transformation à la valeur pour la clientèle, à la croissance, aux marges, aux flux de trésorerie, à la productivité et aux capacités organisationnelles.
Excellentes aptitudes en communication auprès de la haute direction, en animation et en synthèse.
Capacité à remettre en question les pratiques établies de façon constructive et à évoluer dans l’ambiguïté avec rapidité et discernement.
Connaissance des modèles commerciaux internationaux, des environnements de gestion de la relation client (CRM) et de planification des ressources de l’entreprise (ERP), ainsi que des processus clients de bout en bout.
Une expérience dans un environnement industriel, manufacturier, électromécanique ou de technologies interentreprises (B2B) constitue un atout. Une certification reconnue en transformation, en gestion du changement, en Lean, en Six Sigma ou en gestion de programmes constitue un atout.
Maîtrise de l’anglais.

The Executive Vice President (EVP) of Project Management is responsible for leading the company’s overall project management system. This role oversees enterprise-level project strategy, portfolio planning, the execution of major projects, resource allocation, schedule control, budget management, and project delivery performance—ensuring that the company’s strategic projects and business initiatives advance efficiently and systematically toward their established goals.

The position focuses on enterprise-level project governance, the execution of strategic projects, and the management of project delivery. It serves as a key link between the Project Management Office (PMO) and various functions, including business operations, finance, technology, product development, human resources, and other business units. By establishing unified project management standards, execution mechanisms, oversight systems, and performance evaluation frameworks, the EVP enhances project delivery quality, operational efficiency, resource utilization, and cross-functional collaboration, ensuring that project outcomes remain aligned with the company’s long-term strategic objectives.

Core Responsibilities

I. Project Management Strategy and Planning
- Formulate the company’s overarching project management strategy, annual project objectives, and long-term execution plans.
- Develop a project management system aligned with the company’s corporate development strategy.
- Oversee the planning and implementation of the company’s major and strategic projects.
- Establish project management policies, execution standards, and operational guidelines.

III. Execution Management for Major Projects
- Lead the implementation of the company’s core projects and cross-functional strategic initiatives.
- Supervise the full project lifecycle, including initiation, planning, execution, monitoring, and closure.

- Address issues such as project delays, resource shortages, and execution obstacles.
- Establish mechanisms for milestone reviews and periodic project phase acceptance.
- Drive coordination and problem-solving for complex, multi-faceted projects.

IV. Project Resource and Team Management
- Coordinate resource allocation across project managers, project supervisors, and specialized teams.
- Determine project staffing requirements and develop long-term resource plans.
- Optimize project team workloads and personnel utilization rates.
- Adjust personnel, budget, and technical resources based on project priorities.
- Establish performance management and talent development mechanisms for project managers.
- Ensure that key projects are adequately resourced for execution.

V. Project Budgeting and Cost Control
- Oversee the company’s overall project budget and capital expenditure plans.

- Identify risks of budget overruns and drive corrective actions.
- Analyze project cost-benefit and return-on-investment (ROI) performance.
- Enhance project budget transparency and cost-control capabilities.

VI. Project Schedule and Delivery Performance
- Establish a unified system for project schedule management and delivery oversight.
- Monitor key milestones, project completion rates, and delivery quality.

- Regularly assess variances between actual project progress and planned schedules.
- Require project managers to develop recovery plans for delays and performance improvement initiatives.
- Ensure projects are delivered on time, within budget, and in accordance with requirements.

VII. Project Processes and Standardization
- Establish a company-wide project management methodology and execution standards.

- Develop scalable and replicable project management best practices.

- Establish an enterprise-level framework for identifying, assessing, and providing early warnings for project risks.

- Facilitate project risk assessments, root-cause analyses, and the implementation of corrective measures.
- Define standards for project quality reviews and delivery acceptance. - Mitigate the risks of project delays, budget overruns, and delivery failures.

Own and drive the NEMA International transformation roadmap aligned with the Stabilize-Optimize-Scale journey, translating strategy into prioritized initiatives with clear outcomes, milestones and success measures while maintaining visibility of progress and risks to leadership.

Lead an executive-level International Transformation Office that manages the transformation portfolio, governance cadence, dependency view and risk escalation, mobilizing cross-functional workstreams and intervening to resolve ownership gaps, resource constraints or delayed decisions.
Lead adoption of the new international organization and ways of working through change leadership, stakeholder engagement and capability building, while establishing a continuous improvement framework that connects frontline issues to structural business improvements and embeds continuous improvement into leadership accountability.

Minimum 10 years of progressive experience in business transformation, strategy execution, operating-model design, commercial excellence, enterprise program leadership or management consulting.
Bachelor's or Master's degree in Business Administration, Engineering, Strategy, Operations, Information Systems or a related discipline.

Écrivez le prochain chapitre de votre histoire chez ABB.

Ce poste de direction est axé sur la transformation stratégique au sein de la division NEMA International d’ABB et relève du vice-président exécutif, ventes internationales. Il joue un rôle essentiel dans la mise en place d’une plateforme d’affaires internationales évolutive en renforçant l’alignement entre les régions, les secteurs d’activité et les fonctions, en éliminant les obstacles structurels à la croissance et en pilotant la mise en œuvre de la feuille de route Stabiliser-Optimiser-Déployer à grande échelle. Ce poste contribue aux activités de la division Moteurs NEMA du secteur Motion à l’échelle mondiale.

Ce poste exige des déplacements internationaux représentant environ 30 à 40 % du temps de travail.

Vos principales responsabilités seront les suivantes :

Prendre en charge et piloter la feuille de route de transformation de NEMA International, en cohérence avec le parcours Stabiliser-Optimiser-Déployer à grande échelle, en traduisant la stratégie en initiatives prioritaires assorties de résultats, de jalons et de critères de réussite clairs, tout en assurant à la direction une visibilité sur les progrès et les risques.
Agir comme principal point d’intégration entre NEMA International et les secteurs d’activité mondiaux, en établissant des mécanismes de gouvernance et des engagements interfonctionnels qui alignent les priorités en matière de produits, de portefeuille et d’investissements sur les exigences des marchés internationaux, tout en portant à l’attention de la direction les interdépendances critiques qui freinent la croissance.
Piloter la résolution des obstacles systémiques aux interfaces entre les ventes internationales, les opérations mondiales, les TI, les finances, les RH et les autres fonctions de soutien, en regroupant les problèmes isolés en initiatives prioritaires visant leurs causes fondamentales, assorties de responsabilités claires et de résultats mesurables.
Veiller au maintien du modèle opérationnel cible de NEMA International, en s’assurant que les responsabilités organisationnelles, la gouvernance, les processus, les technologies et les capacités évoluent de façon cohérente pour soutenir une croissance internationale rentable, de la stabilisation à l’optimisation, puis au déploiement à grande échelle, tout en concevant l’organisation en fonction de sa croissance et de ses acquisitions futures.
Diriger un bureau de transformation internationale au niveau de la haute direction, responsable du portefeuille de transformation, du rythme de gouvernance, du suivi des interdépendances et du signalement des risques, en mobilisant les chantiers interfonctionnels et en intervenant pour résoudre les lacunes dans l’attribution des responsabilités, les contraintes de ressources ou les retards décisionnels.
Piloter l’adoption de la nouvelle organisation internationale et des nouvelles façons de travailler grâce au leadership du changement, à la mobilisation des parties prenantes et au développement des capacités, tout en établissant un cadre d’amélioration continue qui relie les problèmes de première ligne aux améliorations structurelles des activités et intègre l’amélioration continue aux responsabilités de la direction.

Au moins 10 ans d’expérience avec des responsabilités croissantes en transformation des activités, en exécution de la stratégie, en conception de modèles opérationnels, en excellence commerciale, en direction de programmes d’entreprise ou en conseil en gestion.
Baccalauréat ou maîtrise en administration des affaires, en génie, en stratégie, en gestion des opérations, en systèmes d’information ou dans une discipline connexe.
Expérience dans un rôle interne en stratégie, en transformation, en excellence opérationnelle ou en consultation.
Expérience démontrée dans la direction de transformations complexes et interfonctionnelles touchant plusieurs régions géographiques ou unités d’affaires.
Capacité éprouvée à rallier les parties prenantes de la haute direction et les fonctions autour de priorités communes, sans s’appuyer sur une autorité hiérarchique directe.
Expérience dans la traduction de la stratégie en feuilles de route réalisables, en structures de gouvernance, en mécanismes opérationnels et en résultats mesurables.
Solide sens des affaires et capacité à relier la transformation à la valeur pour la clientèle, à la croissance, aux marges, aux flux de trésorerie, à la productivité et aux capacités organisationnelles.
Excellentes aptitudes en communication auprès de la haute direction, en animation et en synthèse.
Capacité à remettre en question les pratiques établies de façon constructive et à évoluer dans l’ambiguïté avec rapidité et discernement.
Connaissance des modèles commerciaux internationaux, des environnements de gestion de la relation client (CRM) et de planification des ressources de l’entreprise (ERP), ainsi que des processus clients de bout en bout.
Une expérience dans un environnement industriel, manufacturier, électromécanique ou de technologies interentreprises (B2B) constitue un atout. Une certification reconnue en transformation, en gestion du changement, en Lean, en Six Sigma ou en gestion de programmes constitue un atout.
Maîtrise de l’anglais.

Pour en savoir plus sur nous

La division Moteurs NEMA d’ABB commercialise, conçoit et fabrique des moteurs électriques industriels Baldor-Reliance®, principalement en Amérique du Nord. La division mise sur la qualité, la fiabilité et l’efficacité afin d’offrir une gamme complète de moteurs NEMA sur le marché, couvrant la plupart des segments et des applications industriels.

Flexible work arrangements
Competitive Compensation

Education Fund and Dedicated Education Days
Holiday Closure

Introduction:

ICES is seeking a Director, Indigenous Partnerships, Data and Analytic Services to join our Indigenous Partnerships, Data and Analytic Services (IPDA) department. Reporting to the Senior Director, Strategic Partnerships and Digital Services, the Director, in collaboration with ICES leadership, is responsible for the development and delivery of the work of the department at ICES. This includes the developing partnerships, guiding governance, connecting with communities, and developing mutual capacity building with First Nations, Métis, Inuit organizational and health service provider partners across urban, rural, and remote geographies

Responsibilities of the position include, but may not be limited to:

Indigenous Partnership Development:

Accountable for developing, implementing, and managing the Indigenous Partnerships, Data and Analytics (IPDA) department at ICES. This includes facilitating the assertion of representative and diverse First Nations, Inuit, and Métis approaches, perspectives, protocols, and practices to leadership at ICES.
Effectively manage all aspects of performance management for direct reports, including coaching individuals and conducting continuous evaluations to enhance team effectiveness and alignment with departmental goals.
Utilize leadership and project management skills to ensure that departmental initiatives align with ICES' strategic objectives and community needs.

Strategy Management and Operational Planning:

Manage the design and development of an effective and ongoing strategy related to Indigenous data and partnerships. This involves advancing the harmonization of ongoing ICES scientific and corporate strategies with First Nations, Inuit, and Métis requirements and protocols.
Employ analytical and strategic planning skills to assess current practices and develop actionable plans. This includes utilizing data analysis tools and stakeholder feedback to inform strategy development and ensure alignment with community needs and organizational objectives.
Work with cross-functional teams to ensure that the strategy is responsive to evolving Indigenous data sovereignty principles, leveraging collaborative skills to engage stakeholders in the process.
Oversee departmental expenses and recovery of costs by reviewing financial reports and tracking operational expenditures and ensure budget compliance.
Analyze budget requirements and make recommendations for resource allocation, ensuring that financial resources are used efficiently to support research projects and departmental initiatives.

Policy Advisory:

Advise on adapting ICES policies and processes to align with the visions, principles, and requirements of First Nations, Inuit, and Métis Peoples across Ontario. This ensures that all organizational practices are culturally relevant and compliant with community expectations.
Utilize knowledge of Indigenous governance and policy frameworks to facilitate discussions with stakeholders, gathering insights and recommendations for policy adaptation. This involves conducting research and engaging with community leaders to ensure that ICES practices reflect Indigenous perspectives and values.
Prepare policy briefs and reports to communicate recommendations to ICES leadership, ensuring that information is clear and actionable.

Education and Capacity Building:

Educate and provide expertise to internal and external partners regarding First Nations, Inuit, and Métis Peoples' data and data use at ICES. This includes developing training materials and conducting workshops to enhance understanding of Indigenous data sovereignty principles.
Leverage communication and presentation skills to effectively convey complex information, utilizing multimedia tools and resources to engage diverse audiences.
Oversee the development of internal and external capacity-building initiatives, collaborating with educational institutions and community organizations to strengthen partnerships and enhance data literacy.

External Representation:

Represent ICES at external meetings and share ICES’ approach to integrating Indigenous data sovereignty principles. This involves engaging with Indigenous thought leaders to seek guidance on best practices and emerging trends in Indigenous data management.
Utilize networking and relationship-building skills to establish and maintain connections with key external stakeholders, ensuring that ICES remains responsive to community needs and perspectives.
Develop proposals and oversee reporting documents for funders and stakeholders

Team Management and Development:

Manage, coach, and evaluate the team by providing regular feedback and facilitating team-building activities to promote collaboration and alignment with goals, utilizing performance management tools and techniques.
Foster a culture of continuous improvement by identifying training needs, organizing professional development opportunities, and mentoring team members to enhance their skills and career growth, ensuring access to relevant resources and training programs.
Utilize leadership and mentoring skills to enhance departmental effectiveness and individual growth, ensuring alignment with ICES' mission and values by creating an inclusive and supportive team environment.

Other duties as may be assigned within the scope of this position.

Bachelor’s Degree in related field;
At least 8 years of Indigenous community and/or research experience;
Experience working with major health system and Indigenous stakeholders and leaders within Ontario;
A minimum of 5 years management experience;
Demonstrated knowledge of Indigenous cultures and histories in Canada.

Preferred Education, Years of Experience:

Master’s degree in related field.;
Demonstrated knowledge of Indigenous cultures and histories in Canada, through personal lived experiences.

Understanding and experience working with principles of Indigenous data sovereignty.
Familiarity and knowledge of the diversity of First Nation, Inuit, and Métis Peoples.
Recognized leadership in First Nations, Métis, and/or Inuit communities, demonstrating a commitment to cultural competence and community engagement.
Experience working with Provincial, Territorial and/or Federal government and government agencies;
Demonstrated understanding of Indigenous research methodologies and approaches, with an asset being knowledge of quantitative Indigenous health research methodologies.
Demonstrated understanding of strategic planning and program implementation, ensuring alignment with community needs and organizational goals.
Demonstrated project management expertise, including budget and timeline management, to ensure successful delivery of initiatives.
Demonstrated understanding of the health care system, policy development, and planning in Ontario, particularly as it relates to Indigenous health.
Collaborative leadership skills, demonstrating the ability to lead effective teams toward desired outcomes.

Relationship building skills, with a proven ability to foster trust and collaboration among stakeholders.
Flexibility and adaptability to work on multiple projects simultaneously, managing competing priorities effectively.
Demonstrated strategic planning and management skills, with a focus on achieving measurable results and community impact.
